author_name: Yusuf Durachman, Yusuf Durrachman, Yusuf Durrahman
title: Behavioral intention analysis of distance education system using the innovation diffusion theory and technology acceptance model
title_en: Behavioral intention analysis of distance education system using the innovation diffusion theory and technology acceptance model
abstract_en: The Distance Education System (DES) is a learning system by using online application facilities through internet that rapidly adopted in the education sector. However, there has been many obstacles and problems that hinder learning activities. It has been implemented in all level of education in Indonesia even more during pandemic Covid-19. DES is one of the innovations that have been adopted in education sector, hence its kind of technology can influence the intention of learning. The purpose of this study is to measure an individual perception on behavioural intention to use of Distance Education Systems (DES) in the province of DKI Jakarta area. Researchers used a combination of the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Innovation Diffusion Theory (IDT) research models. The sampling technique used is purposive sampling, which only selects the students of Islamic Junior high school (Madrasah Aliyah Negeri/MAN) in the province of DKI Jakarta area. The data analysis method used is PLS-SEM with the product software of SmartPLS 3.3.3. The results of the study indicate that 8 out of 13 hypotheses are accepted. The variable that has the greatest influence on behavioural intention to use is compatibility mediated by perceived usefulness. The results found that three IDT variables (relative advantages, complexity, trialability) have a significant effect on the perceived usefulness variable, then lead to it has a significant relationship on behavioral intention to use. In addition, the two of IDT variable namely compatibility and trialability have significant effect on the perceived ease of use then it has a significant effect on behavioral intention to use. The study found that the behavioural intention to use of DES influenced by the innovation characteristics (IDT) and mediated by the characteristics of technology itself (TAM).

title: Utilization of the Hot-Fit Model to Measure the Success of Information Systems: a Literature Review
title_en: Utilization of the Hot-Fit Model to Measure the Success of Information Systems: a Literature Review
abstract_en: The Human-Organization-Technology Fit (HOTFit) Model has been widely used in evaluating the success of information system (IS) implementation and adoption across various sectors. This research aims to systematically review ten scientific journal articles that utilized the HOT-Fit model in diverse contexts, such as hospitals, government, industry, and education. Employing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach, this article identifies trends, gaps, and contributions of the HOT-Fit model in supporting the evaluation and decisionmaking related to information systems. The analysis results indicate that “human” and “organizational” factors often serve as key determinants of IS success. This research also recommends integrating HOT-Fit with other evaluation methods to enhance the accuracy of evaluation results.

title: Factors Influencing the Continuance Intention of Telemedicine Application Usage Using the Extended Expectation Confirmation Model (EECM)
title_en: Factors Influencing the Continuance Intention of Telemedicine Application Usage Using the Extended Expectation Confirmation Model (EECM)
abstract_en: Telemedicine services have grown rapidly alongside advances in information technology and the increasing need for convenient and fast access to healthcare services. Telemedicine enables users to conduct online medical consultations without physically visiting healthcare facilities. Halodoc is one of the most popular telemedicine platforms in Indonesia, offering various digital health services such as doctor consultations, medication purchases, and laboratory testing. However, user retention remains a challenge, as not all users continue using the application in the long term. This study aims to test and develop the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) by adding two external variables service quality and self-efficacy to explain users' continuance intention in using the Halodoc application. A quantitative approach was employed using a survey method with questionnaires. A sample of 209 respondents was selected through non-probability sampling with a purposive sampling approach, focusing on active Halodoc users in the Jabodetabek area. Data analysis was conducted using PLS-SEM with the SmartPLS software. The results show that the Extended Expectation Confirmation Model (EECM) used in this study is valid and effective in explaining the continuance usage of the Halodoc application. The variables of perceived usefulness, satisfaction, service quality, and self-efficacy significantly influence continuance use intention, with service quality being the most dominant variable. The study proposed nine hypotheses, of which seven were accepted and two rejected. The rejected hypotheses were the effects of confirmation on satisfaction and service quality on satisfaction, which were found to be insignificant due to t-statistic values below the threshold. These findings are expected to serve as a reference for future studies on the adoption of telemedicine health service technologies.

title: Development of web-based spatial information system tourism industry event distribution (case study)
title_en: Development of web-based spatial information system tourism industry event distribution (case study)
abstract_en: In recent years, the number and scope of events in the Asia and Middle East / North Africa region has increased significantly. Events are one of the things that attracts the attention of foreign tourists to come to visit a country as a tourist destination. Refers toMinister of Tourism Regulation Number 2 Year 2017on Guidelines for Venues for Meetings, Incentive Trips, Conventions and Exhibitions, explains that criteria and indicators are needed to increase the competitiveness of venues for meetings, incentive trips, conventions and exhibitions at the regional and global levels. This is done to increase the number of visits, length of stay, and expenditures for domestic and foreign tourists. Therefore, visual indicators or data are needed that can present the location of the event and a list of events in DKI Jakarta. From these problems, this study aims to produce a web-based spatial information system for the distribution of tourism industry events to map event locations in DKI Jakarta. The methodology used in collecting this data is the method of observation, interviews, and literature studies. While the system development methodology uses PHP and MySQL with the Rapid Application Development (RAD) approach and uses the Unified Modeling Language (UML) which is a tool for system description and design, as well as the Google Maps API for digital maps. title: User Experience Design Analysis Using Lean UX Method
title_en: User Experience Design Analysis Using Lean UX Method
abstract_en: Bizmeth is an Android-based application that was created to make it easier for users to build the widest possible business network quickly and easily. Based on the results of observations, it was found that there was a negative response from users related to the experience when using the application both through application comments on Google Playstore and through admin, a decrease in the number of users with the number of installed users as many as 34 and 19 uninstall users, and it was found 6 features that are not yet according to what user needs. In applications, generally, there is an interface that makes it easy for users so that they can be used as needed. Based on these findings, the researcher conducted a study to design the UI/UX of the bizmetch application to meet user needs. The method used is Lean UX. The design process occurs 2 times iteration, in the first iteration it produces 71% positive comments and 29% negative comments, in the second iteration it produces 100% positive comments indicating that the user has received the application interface and the new system flow. The results of this research are in the form of a prototype design of the application that can be used by developers to improve the user experience of the application.

title: Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process: Pendekatan dalam Sistem Pendukung Keputusan Lokasi Coffee Shop
title_en: Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process: Approach in Coffee Shop Location Decision Support Systems
abstract_en: One of the main challenges in distributing zakat is the limited funds available compared to the number of applications for assistance which continues to increase. This condition causes institutions such as BAZNAS to carry out strict selection and determine priorities for aid recipients fairly. In an effort to answer these problems, this research developed a Decision Support System (DSS) using a combination of Random Forest and Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) methods. The Random Forest method is used to classify the eligibility of prospective zakat recipients based on five main criteria, namely income, number of dependents, residence status, history of receiving aid, and nominal application. Meanwhile, the Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) is used to determine the priority level of candidates who have been declared eligible. This research uses data from BAZNAS Bandung City, which was collected through observation and interviews. The evaluation results show that the Random Forest model built has an accuracy rate of 88.98%, with precision and recall each above 93%, indicating high classification performance. Furthermore, the Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) weighting process produces a dominant weight for the income criterion of 0.408, followed by residence status and number of dependents. This system has succeeded in assisting the selection and ranking process of prospective zakat recipients objectively, efficiently and transparently. With this approach, it is hoped that zakat managers can optimize zakat distribution according to priorities to those in need.
